$comment: pclntab  - Go function names + addresses parsed out of the installed CLI binary,
then the strings/constants those functions reference.
proto    - protobuf descriptors embedded in the installed CLI binary.
strings  - plain string-literal search over the installed CLI binary.
feed     - live release feed, re-checkable at any time.
cli      - observed by running the installed CLI.
measured - a live request against the backend, recorded in the code comment.
Confidence: 'confirmed' = read directly from the artifact; 'unresolved' = the
artifact does not say, and a capture of a live authenticated request is needed.
docs/ is not bundled with npm, and this is data rather than prose, so the EN+zh
The `unresolved` list at the end is the entry point for open questions: each is something the artifact does not answer and a live authenticated capture would.

claimRationale: The official client's identity is parameterized per AUTH PROVIDER, not global:
`.GetAuthMethod` exist for X in {CLI, Standalone, IDE, Host, AntigravityHub,
Stubby, GeminiAPIKey}. So 'which product do we claim' is answered by which
credential source we use, and our credentials are the CLI's (see oauth.clientId).

providerHeaderSetsDiffer.evidence: (*CLIAuthProvider).SetHTTPHeaders and (*AntigravityHubAuthProvider).SetHTTPHeaders are each 576 bytes of real work and reference DIFFERENT constants (the CLI one references 'business_agent_platform_paygo'; the hub one references the other OAuth client id). The other five are 32-byte no-ops. The CLI and the hub therefore send different headers — so a header set copied from a hub-shaped client is wrong for us.

internalCodename.note: e.g. 'jetski-standalone-oauth-token' as the keyring service name

feed.note: The binary also embeds this repository path (raw.githubusercontent.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/refs/heads/main/CHANGELOG.md) for its `changelog` subcommand.

namespacesAreDisjoint.consequence: Taking the numeric max across the IDE and CLI feeds compares unrelated numbers. The resolver must read the claimed line only; the other lines are for the freshness gate's cross-check.

unresolved: Whether the backend model-gates on this version is UNPROVEN. It is the one cosmetic
variable with a plausible mechanism (capability gating rather than detection), which
is why it stays in the 'keep' tier while the rest of the cosmetic axis is hygiene.

finding: The CLI contains NO `Antigravity/` literal and no bare `antigravity` product token
anywhere: all 10 `antigravity/` hits are paths, URLs and package names
`os_type=%s` and `%s/%s (%s)` — which read like a UA template — are each referenced
That function also references the endpoint URLs, `auth_method=%s`, `Content-Type`
and the `User-Agent` literal, i.e. it prints a diagnostic dump of identity fields.
They are debug FORMAT STRINGS, not the wire value. (An earlier pass mis-read them as
the UA builder; so, apparently, did the community implementations whose
`antigravity/<ver> <platform>` shape is exactly `%s/%s (%s)` with those three args
filled in. That is a plausible shared origin for the shape we inherited.)
No application function references the `User-Agent` literal at all: all 28 refs are
net/http, grpc, connectrpc and httptest internals. The lowercase `user-agent` literal
IS referenced by application-adjacent code — `genai.buildRequest` (3x) — alongside
`google-genai-sdk/%s`, `gl-go/%s` and `%s %s`. So on the genai SDK path the UA is
`google-genai-sdk/<sdkVersion> gl-go/<goVersion>`, set by Google's own SDK.
`grpc-go/` and `connect-go/` do not appear as literals.

ourCurrentValue.verdict: NOT evidenced for the CLI. Kept on the wire (a Node client sending no UA is its own anomaly, and a speculative replacement is exactly the failure mode this file exists to prevent), but it must not be described as 'the official client string'.

candidates: google-genai-sdk/<ver> gl-go/<ver> (evidenced, but only on the genai SDK path)
no explicit UA at all, i.e. the Go/Node default (the CLI sets none in app code)

`antigravity/cli/<ver> (aidev_client; os_type=macos; arch=arm64; auth_method=consumer)` — NOT confirmed against the artifact, but it is what EVERY live `scripts/verify-*` probe in this repo has sent since the initial commit, and its parenthesized vocabulary (`aidev_client`, `os_type=`, `auth_method=`) is exactly what the binary's string blob contains. So it is a worked-in-practice CLI-shaped candidate, while the `src/` UA (`antigravity/<ver> <platform>`) is a different shape used on the real data plane. The two disagreeing is itself a finding.
captureRecipe: The UA needs a live authenticated request. Options, cheapest first:
— CLOUD_CODE_URL is a real endpoint override (`[AuthProvider] UpdateEndpointURL
called with CLOUD_CODE_URL`), so a local listener sees the request in the clear.
so the capture must decode HTTP/2 + HPACK — use a real gRPC server, not a raw socket.
Note the CLI writes its logs to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log but does NOT
log request headers at the default verbosity, so the logs do not answer this.

wireFieldNameNote: The MESSAGE is `ClientMetadata`; the FIELD that carries it is named `metadata`.
There is NO evidenced `metadata` field on the generate (data-plane) request, which is
why the data plane keeps its envelope (`userAgent`/`requestType`) as the carrier and
does not gain an unverified field.
The snake_case name `client_metadata` occurs ZERO times in the binary.
corrections: The invariant 'Client-Metadata must only transmit ideType' is VOID. It came from a
live INVALID_ARGUMENT, but the value under test was `"MACOS"`, which is not a member
of the Platform enum above. A bad enum VALUE is not a forbidden FIELD.
`platform` takes the enum NAME (`DARWIN_ARM64`), a different vocabulary from the UA's
`darwin/arm64` token. Both exist; conflating them is what produced `"MACOS"`.

ideType.note: The CLI's own IdeType is injected through its auth provider and was not captured. `GEMINI_CLI` is the enum's newer CLI value and is the alternative to settle by capture; the established working value is kept rather than guessed.

platform.note: platform is pinned to darwin/arm64 (see AGENTS.md), so the enum takes its arm64 member.

liveCheck.result: 200 — the backend accepts `{ideType, ideVersion, platform}` on loadCodeAssist
why: This is the one change this round makes to the LOGIN/ONBOARDING path, where a
wrong field breaks new accounts instead of degrading a generation, so it was
measured rather than reasoned about. The script also runs the legacy
`{ ideType }` body as a control, so a future failure is attributable: if the
current body is rejected while the legacy one is accepted, the added fields are
the cause and `platform` is what to drop.
`dsh-agy verify` cannot answer this — it refreshes the token and calls
googleapis.com/oauth2/v1/userinfo, which never reaches the Cloud Code backend.

omitted.why: no captured value; an absent field is merely incomplete, a wrong one is a new anomaly

absentFromBothBinaries.note: Zero occurrences in the CLI binary AND in the IDE language server. Anything here is community-invented, including two headers this project used to send.

x-goog-api-client.note: An SDK-level header, and it IS official — do not delete it. Our value pool (`google-cloud-sdk vscode*/...`) does NOT match the CLI's SDK-shaped value; recorded as a mismatch rather than silently changed.

X-Aicode-Prompt-Id.note: App-level custom header, real and unmodelled by us.

X-Aicode-Request-Id.note: The nearest official analogue of the request id we carry in the body.

unresolved: Whether the X-Aicode-* trio is also sent on the GENERATE path. It is only evidenced on
fetchAvailableModels, so we send none of them: adding a header on a guess is the
behaviour this file exists to stop.

thoughtSignatureSentinel.finding: The sentinel lives in the TRAJECTORY->CHAT CONVERSION (i.e. history replay), the model-output retry, and checkpointing — not in one-per-functionCall emission. This is the first direct evidence on the placement question; confirming whether it covers only the first functionCall still needs one live parallel-tool turn.

rejections.finding: This is the official enumeration of why the backend declines to serve. Note that only VALIDATION_REQUIRED is one we have ever seen, and that UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT / GOOGLE_TOS_NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_CLIENT are the client-identity members — the surface a client-shape check would actually use. DASHER_USER and BYOID_USER name account TYPES, i.e. enforcement that no amount of impersonation addresses.

oauth.clientIdNote: Identical to our AGY_CLIENT_ID. Public client credentials embedded in the official artifact (see AGENTS.md), not a project secret.

secondClientId.note: A SECOND OAuth client exists in the same binary, alongside two GOCSPX- client secrets. Our pair (1071006060591-... / <AGY_CLIENT_SECRET in src/oauth/constants.ts>) is one of them. Do NOT delete ours; do not assume the other is interchangeable.

oauth.store: OS keyring, service `jetski-standalone-oauth-token`, falling back to a file; `JETSKI_OAUTH_TOKEN` overrides from the environment.

$comment: Where AGY_ENDPOINT_FALLBACKS differs from what the artifact names. Declared here
so the gate fails on UNDECLARED deviations only, and so the difference is a
recorded fact rather than a silent inheritance from another implementation.

extraInOurs.finding: Occurs exactly ONCE in the CLI binary, and that occurrence is a SUBSTRING of `https://preprod-daily-cloudcode-pa.sandbox.googleapis.com` (a naive search reports it as present; a boundary-aware one does not). It is absent from the IDE language server entirely. It DOES resolve in DNS, so it is a real Google host that the official client simply does not name — not dead weight, but also not evidence.
extraInOurs.verdict: kept: it resolves and it is the third of four fallbacks, so removing a working hop to satisfy a name list would be the tail wagging the dog

missingFromOurs.finding: Named by the official CLI, and it resolves.
missingFromOurs.verdict: NOT added: the fallback order is measured-load-bearing (AGENTS.md), so a fifth hop belongs in its own change with its own measurement, not in an identity-recording commit

endpoints.note: `preprod-daily-...` was initially recorded as the only sandbox host because the first pass read it out of the `printDebugInfo` string blob; a boundary-aware scan over the whole binary is what settled it.

environment.note: `AGY_ENABLE_HUB` confirms a hub mode exists behind a flag, which is the concrete form of the CLI-vs-hub product question.

cliOperational.architecture: `agy` is a client that spawns a LANGUAGE SERVER process; the LS does the upstream work and logs klog-style to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-<ts>.log with a `Language server version: <v>` line.
cliOperational.noLoginSubcommand: Login is the interactive `/login` slash command, not a subcommand — so there is no non-interactive way to make the official CLI authenticated without injecting a token.
cliOperational.changelogIsEmbedded: `agy changelog` prints through a dead HTTPS_PROXY, i.e. it is served from the embedded copy; the live URL is only what it would refresh from.
cliOperational.note: This machine's CLI is NOT logged in ('You are not logged into Antigravity'), which is why every wire-level capture above is still 'unresolved' rather than 'confirmed'.
